questionText: 17th of month is Saturday. First day of month was?
hints: The same day of the week comes back every 7 days. Use this to jump backwards from the date you know.
Take 7 away from 17, and then 7 again, to find earlier Saturdays. Then count back the last few days to the 1st.

Similar example: the 20th is a Wednesday. Going back in 7s, the 13th and the 6th are also Wednesdays. Counting back from the 6th: the 5th is Tuesday, the 4th Monday, the 3rd Sunday, the 2nd Saturday and the 1st Friday.

stepByStep.text: Go back 7 days. The 10th is also a Saturday.
Go back 7 more days. The 3rd is also a Saturday.
Count back from the 3rd: the 2nd is a Friday and the 1st is a Thursday.
So the first day of the month was Thursday.

misconceptions.A: Friday is the 2nd, the day before Saturday the 3rd. Go back one more day to reach the 1st.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The 3rd is a Saturday, so the 2nd is Friday and the 1st is Thursday.
misconceptions.C: Check your counting back. The 3rd is a Saturday, so the 2nd is Friday and the 1st is the day before that.
misconceptions.D: Sunday comes after Saturday. Here we go backwards from Saturday the 3rd to reach the 1st.

questionText: At half past six, angle between hour and minute hand?
hints: On a clock the hour hand does not sit still. It creeps forward as the minutes pass. Find where each hand points, then find the gap between them.
The gap between two neighbouring numbers on a clock is 30°. At half past six the minute hand is on 6. Think about where the hour hand is between 6 and 7.

Similar example: at 20 minutes past 8, the minute hand is on 4. In 60 minutes the hour hand moves 30°, so in 20 minutes it moves 10° past the 8. From 4 to 8 is 4 × 30 = 120°. The angle is 120 + 10 = 130°.

stepByStep.text: The 12 numbers on a clock share a full turn of 360°. So each gap between numbers is 30°.
At half past six the minute hand points exactly at 6.
Half an hour has passed since 6 o'clock, so the hour hand has moved halfway from 6 to 7.
Half of one gap is the angle between the hands. The angle is 15°.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The hour hand is half a gap past 6, and half of 30° is 15°.
misconceptions.B: Check the size of one gap. Each gap between clock numbers is 30°, and the hour hand is half a gap past 6.
misconceptions.C: This is one full gap. The hour hand is only halfway from 6 to 7, so the angle is half of this.
misconceptions.D: This is one and a half gaps. The hour hand is only half a gap away from the minute hand at 6.

questionText: In 300 seconds the minute hand moves ___ degrees?
hints: Change the seconds into minutes first. Then think about how far the minute hand turns in one minute.
There are 60 seconds in a minute, so find 300 ÷ 60. The minute hand goes all the way round, 360°, in 60 minutes.
Similar example: in 900 seconds, 900 ÷ 60 = 15 minutes pass. The minute hand turns 360 ÷ 60 = 6° each minute. So it turns 15 × 6 = 90°.

stepByStep.text: Change 300 seconds into minutes.
The minute hand makes a full turn of 360° in 60 minutes. Find its turn in 1 minute.
In 5 minutes it turns 5 times as much. The minute hand moves 30 degrees.

misconceptions.A: This is half of 300. First change 300 seconds to 5 minutes, then use 6° for each minute.
misconceptions.B: That is the turn in 10 minutes. 300 seconds is only 5 minutes.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 300 seconds is 5 minutes, and 5 × 6 = 30.
misconceptions.D: This is half of the real turn. The minute hand moves 6° every minute, and 5 minutes pass.

questionText: 1st Jan 2006 = Sunday. 1st Jan 2010?
hints: An ordinary year has 365 days, which is 52 full weeks and 1 extra day. So the same date moves forward one weekday each year, and two after a leap year.
Go one year at a time from 1st January 2006. Check which of the years 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009 is a leap year.

Similar example: 1st January 2014 was a Wednesday. 2014 and 2015 are ordinary years, so 1st January 2015 is a Thursday and 1st January 2016 is a Friday. 2016 is a leap year, so the day moves on by 2: 1st January 2017 is a Sunday.

stepByStep.text: An ordinary year is 52 weeks and 1 day, so a date moves on by 1 weekday.
2006 is an ordinary year, so 1st January 2007 is a Monday. 2007 is ordinary too, so 1st January 2008 is a Tuesday.
2008 is a leap year with 366 days, so the day moves on by 2. 1st January 2009 is a Thursday.
2009 is an ordinary year. So 1st January 2010 is a Friday.

misconceptions.A: This moves one day too many. Only 2008 is a leap year, so the day moves 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5 days on from Sunday.
misconceptions.B: This moves 4 days, one for each year. 2008 is a leap year, so it adds one extra day.
misconceptions.C: That is the day one year later, in 2007. Keep going for all four years.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The day moves 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5 days on from Sunday, which is Friday.

questionText: Teacher: angle between hands=45°. What time?
hints: Each gap between numbers on a clock is 30°. Remember that the hour hand creeps forward as the minutes pass. Test each time.
Start with the half-past times. The minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between two numbers. Count the gaps between the hands.

Similar example: what is the angle at 3:30? The minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4. From the hour hand to 4 is half a gap, 15°. From 4 to 6 is 2 × 30 = 60°. The angle is 15 + 60 = 75°.

stepByStep.text: Each gap between clock numbers is 30°.
At 7:30 the minute hand is on 6. The hour hand is halfway between 7 and 8.
From 6 to 7 is one gap of 30°. From 7 to the hour hand is half a gap, 15°.
Add them. The angle is 45°, so the time is 07:30.

misconceptions.A: At 1:15 the minute hand is on 3 and the hour hand is a little past 1. That angle is more than 45°. Try a half-past time.
misconceptions.B: At 2:30 the hands are three and a half gaps apart, which is 105°. Look for hands one and a half gaps apart.
misconceptions.C: At 8:30 the hands are two and a half gaps apart, which is 75°. Look for hands one and a half gaps apart.
misconceptions.D: Yes! At 7:30 the hands are one and a half gaps apart, and 30 + 15 = 45.

questionText: Weeks in 8×7×6×5×4×3×2×1 minutes?
hints: Change minutes into hours, hours into days, and days into weeks. Take it one unit at a time.
First multiply out the product to get the number of minutes. Then divide by 60 to change the minutes into hours.
Similar example: how many weeks are in 20160 minutes? 20160 ÷ 60 = 336 hours. 336 ÷ 24 = 14 days. 14 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks.

stepByStep.text: Multiply out the minutes.
Change minutes to hours.
Change hours to days.
Change days to weeks. There are 4 weeks.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 40320 minutes is 672 hours, which is 28 days, and 28 ÷ 7 = 4.
misconceptions.B: Check the last step. The minutes make 28 days, and 28 ÷ 7 gives the weeks.
misconceptions.C: Check the multiplication first. The product is 40320 minutes, which is 672 hours.
misconceptions.D: This is one week too many. The minutes make 28 days, and 7 days make a week.

questionText: It is 4:30pm on April 15th. Minute hand turns 30 times. What date and time?
hints: One full turn of the minute hand takes one hour. So count the turns as hours and move the clock forward.
30 turns means 30 hours. Split 30 hours into one full day of 24 hours and the hours left over.
Similar example: it is 9:00 am on 3rd May and the minute hand turns 28 times. That is 28 hours, and 24 + 4 = 28. After 24 hours it is 9:00 am on 4th May. Four more hours make it 1:00 pm on 4th May.

stepByStep.text: Each full turn of the minute hand is 1 hour. So 30 turns is 30 hours.
Split 30 hours into 1 day and some hours.
24 hours after 4:30 pm on 15th April is 4:30 pm on 16th April.
6 hours after that is 10:30 pm. So it is 10:30pm, 16th April.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 30 turns is 30 hours: one full day and 6 hours more.
misconceptions.B: After full turns the minute hand is back where it started, on the 6. So the time must end in 30 minutes.
misconceptions.C: This adds 42 hours. 30 turns is 30 hours: one full day and 6 more hours.
misconceptions.D: This moves on many days. 30 turns of the minute hand is only 30 hours, a little more than one day.

questionText: Time 2023 minutes after 12:00am on 2nd March 2023?
hints: Change the minutes into hours and minutes. Then see whether the hours go past one full day.
Divide 2023 by 60 to get the hours and the leftover minutes. Remember that a day has 24 hours.
Similar example: 1500 minutes after 12:00 am on 5th June. 1500 ÷ 60 = 25 hours. 24 hours takes us to 12:00 am on 6th June, and 1 more hour makes it 1:00 am on 6th June.

stepByStep.text: 60 minutes make an hour. 33 hours use up 1980 minutes.
Find the minutes left over. So 2023 minutes is 33 hours 43 minutes.
Split 33 hours into 1 day and some hours.
24 hours after 12:00 am on 2nd March is 12:00 am on 3rd March.
9 hours 43 minutes later it is 3rd March 9:43 am.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 2023 minutes is 33 hours 43 minutes: one full day, then 9 hours 43 minutes more.
misconceptions.B: That is only 21 hours 43 minutes after midnight. 2023 minutes is 33 hours 43 minutes, more than a full day.
misconceptions.C: The date is right, but 9 hours after midnight is still morning.
misconceptions.D: This goes one day too far. 33 hours is one full day and 9 hours.

questionText: Angle between hour and minute hand at 8:30 am?
hints: On a clock the hour hand does not sit still. It creeps forward as the minutes pass. Find where each hand points, then count the gaps between them.
Each gap between clock numbers is 30°. At 8:30 the minute hand is on 6. Think about where the hour hand is between 8 and 9.
Similar example: at 2:30 the minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 2 and 3. From the hour hand to 3 is half a gap, 15°. From 3 to 6 is 3 × 30 = 90°. The angle is 15 + 90 = 105°.

stepByStep.text: Each gap between clock numbers is 30°.
At 8:30 the minute hand is on 6. The hour hand is halfway between 8 and 9.
From 6 to 8 is two gaps.
The hour hand is half a gap, 15°, past 8.
The angle is 75°, which is not listed. So the answer is none of these.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The angle is 60° + 15° = 75°, and 75° is not one of the angles given.
misconceptions.B: Check the half gap. The hour hand is 15° past 8, and the two full gaps make 60°.
misconceptions.C: This counts three full gaps, as if the hour hand were on 9. At 8:30 it is only halfway from 8 to 9.
misconceptions.D: Check the adding. Two gaps make 60°, and the half gap adds 15° more.

questionText: Republic Day 2023 = Thursday. Which year on Tuesday?
hints: Republic Day is 26th January. Each ordinary year the day moves forward by 1, and by 2 when a 29th February falls in between.
Go year by year from 26th January 2023. Watch for the leap year 2024: its extra day, 29th February, comes after Republic Day 2024.
Similar example: 26th January 2015 was a Monday. In 2016 it is a Tuesday. From January 2016 to January 2017 we pass 29th February 2016, so it moves 2 days to a Thursday. In 2018 it is a Friday.

stepByStep.text: Republic Day is 26th January. In an ordinary year the same date moves on by 1 weekday.
From 2023 to 2024 there is no leap day in between. So 26th January 2024 is a Friday.
From 2024 to 2025 we pass 29th February 2024, so the day moves on by 2. 26th January 2025 is a Sunday.
Then 2026 gives Monday and 2027 gives Tuesday.
So Republic Day falls on a Tuesday in 2027.

misconceptions.A: In 2026 it falls on a Monday. Go one more year.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The days go Friday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday for 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.
misconceptions.C: In 2028 it falls on a Wednesday. That is one year too far.
misconceptions.D: In 2025 it falls on a Sunday. Keep moving forward one day each year.

questionText: 10:30am on 21st April 2024. Minute hand turns 42 times. Date and time?
hints: One full turn of the minute hand takes one hour. So count the turns as hours and move the clock forward.
42 turns means 42 hours. Split 42 hours into one full day of 24 hours and the hours left over.

Similar example: it is 7:00 am on 10th July and the minute hand turns 40 times. That is 40 hours, and 24 + 16 = 40. After 24 hours it is 7:00 am on 11th July. Sixteen more hours make it 11:00 pm on 11th July.

stepByStep.text: Each full turn of the minute hand is 1 hour. So 42 turns is 42 hours.
Split 42 hours into 1 day and some hours.
24 hours after 10:30 am on 21st April is 10:30 am on 22nd April.
12 hours more makes it 10:30 pm on 22nd April. There are still 6 hours to add.
6 hours after 10:30 pm is 4:30 am the next day. So it is 23rd Apr 4:30am.

misconceptions.A: This goes too far. 42 hours is one full day and 18 hours, which ends early on the 23rd.
misconceptions.B: The time is right but the date is one day too late. 42 hours is less than two full days.
misconceptions.C: This adds only 34 hours. 42 turns of the minute hand is 42 hours.
misconceptions.D: Yes! 42 hours is one full day and 18 hours more, which reaches 4:30 am on the 23rd.

questionText: Independence Day 2024 = Thursday. Which year on Wednesday?
hints: Independence Day is 15th August. Each ordinary year the day moves forward by 1, and by 2 when a 29th February falls in between.
Go year by year from 15th August 2024. Watch for the next leap year, 2028: its 29th February makes the day jump by 2.
Similar example: 15th August 2014 was a Friday. In 2015 it is a Saturday. From August 2015 to August 2016 we pass 29th February 2016, so it moves 2 days to a Monday. In 2017 it is a Tuesday.

stepByStep.text: Independence Day is 15th August. In an ordinary year the same date moves on by 1 weekday.
So 2025 gives Friday, 2026 gives Saturday and 2027 gives Sunday.
From August 2027 to August 2028 we pass 29th February 2028, so the day moves on by 2. 15th August 2028 is a Tuesday.
One more year gives Wednesday. So Independence Day falls on a Wednesday in 2029.

misconceptions.A: In 2028 it falls on a Tuesday, because the leap day makes the day jump on from Sunday. Go one more year.
misconceptions.B: In 2030 it falls on a Thursday. That is one year too far.
misconceptions.C: In 2031 it falls on a Friday. Count on from Thursday one year at a time, with a jump of 2 for 2028.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The days go Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Tuesday, Wednesday for 2025 to 2029.

questionText: Bus from Pune to Mumbai every 36 min from 7am. Arrive 8:50am. Next bus?
hints: List the bus times one after another. The next bus is the first one that leaves after you arrive.
Start at 7:00 am and keep adding 36 minutes: 7:36 am, and so on. Stop when you pass 8:50 am.
Similar example: buses leave every 25 minutes from 6:00 am, and you arrive at 7:20 am. The buses leave at 6:00, 6:25, 6:50, 7:15 and 7:40. The 7:15 bus has gone, so the next bus is at 7:40 am.

stepByStep.text: The buses leave at 7:00 am, 7:36 am, 8:12 am and 8:48 am.
The 8:48 am bus has just left when you arrive at 8:50 am.
Add 36 minutes to 8:48 am. 48 and 36 make 84 minutes, which is 1 hour 24 minutes.
So the next bus is at 9:24 am.

misconceptions.A: This is not one of the bus times. List them from 7:00 am, adding 36 minutes each time.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The bus before leaves at 8:48 am, and 36 minutes later is 9:24 am.
misconceptions.C: Check your list of bus times. After 8:48 am, add 36 minutes to find the next one.
misconceptions.D: This is too late. A bus leaves at 8:48 am, and the next one is only 36 minutes after that.

questionText: If it takes 10 seconds to print a picture, how many pictures can be printed in half an hour?
hints: The two times are in different units. Change them to the same unit before you divide.
Half an hour is 30 minutes. Find how many pictures are printed in 1 minute first.
Similar example: a machine takes 15 seconds to fill a bottle. In 1 minute it fills 60 ÷ 15 = 4 bottles. In a quarter of an hour, which is 15 minutes, it fills 15 × 4 = 60 bottles.

stepByStep.text: Find the pictures printed in 1 minute, which is 60 seconds.
Half an hour is 30 minutes.
Multiply the pictures per minute by 30. So 180 pictures can be printed.

misconceptions.A: 30 is the number of minutes in half an hour. In each of those minutes 6 pictures are printed.
misconceptions.B: This multiplies 60 by 10. Divide instead: 60 ÷ 10 gives 6 pictures a minute, then multiply by 30 minutes.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 6 pictures a minute for 30 minutes makes 6 × 30 = 180.
misconceptions.D: This is 30 × 10. Each minute gives 6 pictures, so multiply 30 by 6.

questionText: A bell rings after every 35 minutes. If it rang for the first time at 9:00 am, when will it ring for the 5th time?
hints: Count the gaps between rings, not the rings. The first ring happens at the start, before any gap has passed.
From the 1st ring to the 5th ring there are 4 gaps. Find how many minutes 4 gaps of 35 minutes make.
Similar example: a bell rings every 25 minutes, first at 8:00 am. The 4th ring comes after 3 gaps: 3 × 25 = 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes. So it rings for the 4th time at 9:15 am.

stepByStep.text: From the 1st ring to the 5th ring there are 4 gaps.
Find the time for 4 gaps.
140 minutes is 2 hours 20 minutes.
2 hours 20 minutes after 9:00 am is 11:20 am.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 4 gaps of 35 minutes make 140 minutes, which is 2 hours 20 minutes after 9:00 am.
misconceptions.B: Write the ring times: 9:00, 9:35, 10:10, 10:45 and then the 5th. Each is 35 minutes after the one before.
misconceptions.C: Check the ring times one by one. Add 35 minutes four times, starting from 9:00 am.
misconceptions.D: This adds 5 gaps of 35 minutes. From the 1st ring to the 5th there are only 4 gaps.

questionText: A train left Pune at quarter past eight in the morning and reached Mumbai at quarter to 1 in the afternoon. If the actual duration is 3 hours 40 min, by how many minutes was the train late?
hints: First find how long the journey really took. Then compare it with how long it should take.
Write the times as clock times: quarter past eight is 8:15 am and quarter to 1 is 12:45 pm. Find the time between them.

Similar example: a bus leaves at quarter past nine and arrives at half past twelve. From 9:15 to 12:15 is 3 hours, and 15 minutes more makes 3 hours 15 minutes. If the trip should take 2 hours 45 minutes, the bus is 30 minutes late.

stepByStep.text: Quarter past eight is 8:15 am. Quarter to 1 is 12:45 pm.
From 8:15 am to 12:15 pm is 4 hours. Then 30 minutes more takes us to 12:45 pm. The journey took 4 hours 30 minutes.
Change to minutes. 4 hours 30 minutes is 270 minutes.
The journey should take 3 hours 40 minutes, which is 220 minutes.
Subtract. The train was late by 50 min.

misconceptions.A: Check the journey time. From 8:15 am to 12:45 pm is 4 hours 30 minutes. Then take away 3 hours 40 minutes.
misconceptions.B: Check the subtraction. 4 hours 30 minutes is 270 minutes and 3 hours 40 minutes is 220 minutes.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The journey took 270 minutes instead of 220 minutes, and 270 − 220 = 50.
misconceptions.D: Quarter to 1 means 15 minutes before 1 o'clock, which is 12:45. Find the journey time from 8:15 to 12:45.

questionText: Priya's watch is 10 minutes slow and Kriya's watch is 5 minutes fast. If Kriya's watch is 3:45 pm, what is the time in Priya's watch?
hints: A fast watch shows a later time than the real time. A slow watch shows an earlier time. Find the real time first.
Kriya's watch is 5 minutes fast, so the real time is 5 minutes before 3:45 pm. Work that out first.
Similar example: Ravi's watch is 10 minutes fast and shows 6:20. So the real time is 6:10. Meena's watch is 15 minutes slow, so it shows 15 minutes before 6:10, which is 5:55.

stepByStep.text: Kriya's watch is 5 minutes fast. So the real time is 5 minutes before 3:45 pm, which is 3:40 pm.
Priya's watch is 10 minutes slow. So it shows 10 minutes before the real time.
Take 10 minutes from 3:40 pm. Priya's watch shows 3:30 pm.

misconceptions.A: This adds both amounts. A fast watch is ahead, so go back 5 minutes for the real time, then back 10 more for the slow watch.
misconceptions.B: This is the real time. Priya's watch is 10 minutes behind it.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The real time is 3:40 pm, and a watch that is 10 minutes slow shows 3:30 pm.
misconceptions.D: This adds 5 minutes. Kriya's watch is fast, so the real time is earlier than 3:45 pm.

questionText: A clock loses 10 minutes every hour. It was set correctly at 1:00 am. What time will this clock show when the actual time is 6:00 am?
hints: A clock that loses time falls further behind every hour. Find how many hours pass, then how much time is lost in total.
Count the hours from 1:00 am to 6:00 am. The clock loses 10 minutes in each of those hours.
Similar example: a clock loses 6 minutes every hour and is set right at 2:00 pm. At 7:00 pm, 5 hours have passed. It has lost 5 × 6 = 30 minutes, so it shows 6:30 pm.

stepByStep.text: Count the hours from 1:00 am to 6:00 am.
The clock loses 10 minutes in each hour.
The clock is 50 minutes behind 6:00 am. So it shows 5:10 am.

misconceptions.A: This adds the 50 minutes. A clock that loses time is behind, so go back 50 minutes from 6:00 am.
misconceptions.B: Yes! In 5 hours the clock loses 50 minutes, and 50 minutes before 6:00 am is 5:10 am.
misconceptions.C: This is only 10 minutes behind. The clock loses 10 minutes in each of the 5 hours.
misconceptions.D: This is 60 minutes behind. Only 5 hours pass, so the clock loses 5 × 10 = 50 minutes.

questionText: A watch gains 5 min every hour. It was set correctly at noon. What is the actual time when this watch shows quarter past three?
hints: A watch that gains time runs ahead. In one real hour it moves forward more than 60 minutes. Think about how far the watch moves in each real hour.
In 1 real hour this watch moves 65 minutes. From noon to quarter past three the watch has moved 3 hours 15 minutes. Change that to minutes.

Similar example: a watch gains 10 minutes every hour and is set right at noon. In each real hour it moves 70 minutes. When it shows 2:20 pm it has moved 140 minutes, and 140 ÷ 70 = 2. So 2 real hours have passed and the real time is 2:00 pm.

stepByStep.text: In 1 real hour the watch moves 5 minutes extra.
From noon to quarter past three, the watch has moved 3 hours 15 minutes.
See how many lots of 65 minutes fit in 195 minutes.
So 3 real hours have passed since noon. The actual time is 3:00 pm.

misconceptions.A: Yes! In 3 real hours the watch gains 15 minutes, so it shows 3:15 pm when the real time is 3:00 pm.
misconceptions.B: This takes off only 5 minutes. The watch gains 5 minutes in every hour, and 3 hours have passed.
misconceptions.C: This takes off 30 minutes. In 3 real hours the watch gains 3 × 5 = 15 minutes.
misconceptions.D: This adds 5 minutes. A watch that gains time is ahead, so the real time is earlier than 3:15 pm.

questionText: How many leap years are there between 1990 and 2004?
hints: A leap year comes once every 4 years, and its number divides by 4 exactly. The word between means the two end years are not counted.
Find the first year after 1990 that divides by 4 exactly. Then keep adding 4, stopping before 2004.
Similar example: leap years between 2010 and 2030. The first is 2012, then 2016, 2020, 2024 and 2028. That makes 5 leap years.

stepByStep.text: 1990 does not divide by 4 exactly, but 1992 does.
Keep adding 4 years: 1992, 1996, 2000. The next one would be 2004.
2004 is an end year, so it is not between 1990 and 2004.
The leap years between them are 1992, 1996 and 2000. That is 3 leap years.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The leap years between 1990 and 2004 are 1992, 1996 and 2000.
misconceptions.B: This also counts 2004. The word between leaves out the end years, so stop at 2000.
misconceptions.C: This counts too many. Leap years come once every 4 years: 1992, 1996 and 2000.
misconceptions.D: This counts every second year. Leap years come once every 4 years, starting here with 1992.

questionText: If the school vacation lasted from 17th April to 3rd June, how long was the vacation?
hints: Count the days month by month: the days left in April, all of May, and the days in June. Remember how many days each month has.
April has 30 days. Count the vacation days in April from the 17th to the 30th, and include the 17th itself.
Similar example: a camp runs from 20th June to 5th July. June has 30 days, so June gives 30 − 20 + 1 = 11 days. July gives 5 days. The camp lasts 11 + 5 = 16 days.

stepByStep.text: April has 30 days. From the 17th to the 30th, counting the 17th too, there are 14 days.
May has 31 days.
June gives 3 days, from the 1st to the 3rd.
Add the three parts. The vacation was 48 days.

misconceptions.A: Check the days in each month. April gives 14 days, May gives 31 and June gives 3.
misconceptions.B: This leaves out the first day. The 17th of April is part of the vacation, so April gives 14 days, not 13.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 14 days in April, 31 in May and 3 in June make 14 + 31 + 3 = 48.
misconceptions.D: This is one day too many. Check that May has 31 days and June gives just 3.

questionText: The school vacation began on 22nd April and lasted for 40 days. When did the school reopen?
hints: Count the vacation days month by month. The school reopens on the day after the last vacation day.
April has 30 days. Count the vacation days in April from the 22nd to the 30th, including the 22nd. Then see how many of the 40 days are left for May.

Similar example: a holiday begins on 25th June and lasts 20 days. June has 30 days, so June gives 30 − 25 + 1 = 6 days. That leaves 20 − 6 = 14 days in July, so the last holiday is 14th July. School reopens on 15th July.

stepByStep.text: April gives the days from the 22nd to the 30th, counting the 22nd too.
Find how many vacation days are left after April.
May has exactly 31 days, so the last day of the vacation is 31st May.
The school reopens the next day, on 1st June.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The 40 days end on 31st May, so school reopens the next day.
misconceptions.B: 31st May is the last day of the vacation. School reopens the day after.
misconceptions.C: This is one day late. Count 22nd April as the first vacation day, so April gives 9 days.
misconceptions.D: This goes backwards from April. The vacation moves forward 40 days, through May.

questionText: A train leaves Pune station at 17:20 on the 24-hour clock. What is this time on the 12-hour clock?
hints: On the 24-hour clock, hours bigger than 12 are afternoon or evening times.
Take 12 away from the hours: 17 - 12. The minutes stay the same.
Example: 14:35 on the 24-hour clock. 14 - 12 = 2, so it is 2:35 pm.

questionText: How many days are there altogether in the months of June and July?
hints: You need to remember how many days each month has. The knuckle trick or the rhyme 'Thirty days has September' can help.
June has 30 days. How many days does July have?
Example: December has 31 days and January has 31 days. Together they have 31 + 31 = 62 days.

misconceptions.C: This takes both months as 31 days. June has only 30 days.
misconceptions.D: This is too few. June has 30 days and July has 31 days.

questionText: How many days are there in February 2028?
hints: February is the only month whose length changes. It depends on whether the year is a leap year.

If 9th = Monday, then 2nd = Monday, so 1st = Sunday. April starts on Sunday.
The first 2 days (Sunday and Monday) occur 5 times: Sundays on 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 and Mondays on 2, 9, 16, 23, 30.

stepByStep.text: April = 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 days. Two days occur 5 times.
9 Apr = Monday → 2 Apr = Monday → 1 Apr = Sunday
First 2 days of the month (Sun, Mon) occur 5 times.

misconceptions.B: Monday occurs 5 times but Tuesday only occurs 4 times
misconceptions.C: Only 2 days can occur 5 times in a 30-day month, not 3
misconceptions.D: The answer IS Sunday and Monday

questionText: A train departs at 09:45 and the journey takes 4 hours 35 minutes. At what time does it arrive?
hints: Add 4 hours 35 minutes to 9:45.
Hours: 9 + 4 = 13. Minutes: 45 + 35 = 80. But 80 minutes = 1 hour 20 minutes!
13 hours + 1 hour 20 minutes = 14:20 = 2:20 PM.

stepByStep.text: Add hours: 9 + 4 = 13
Add minutes: 45 + 35 = 80 = 1 hour 20 min

misconceptions.A: Wrote 1:80 PM — there's no such time! Minutes can't exceed 59.
misconceptions.C: This is actually the same answer in 24-hour format (14:20 = 2:20 PM)
misconceptions.D: Forgot to carry the extra hour from 80 minutes

questionText: Teacher's Day (5th September) 2016 was a Monday. On which day was Christmas celebrated that year?
hints: Count days from 5 Sep to 25 Dec: Sep(25) + Oct(31) + Nov(30) + Dec(25) = 111.
111 ÷ 7 = 15 weeks + 6 days.
Monday + 6 = Sunday.

questionText: Rahul celebrated his 5th birthday on 3rd August 2014 which was a Sunday. Which birthday will fall on Thursday?
questionLatex: \text{3 Aug 2014 = Sun. Which birthday on Thu?}
hints: Each year the same date moves forward by 1 weekday, or by 2 when a 29th February falls in between. Follow the birthdays one year at a time.
Start with 3rd August 2015, the 6th birthday. Then check whether a leap day comes before 3rd August 2016.

Similar example: Asha's 4th birthday is on 10th September 2018, a Monday. Her 5th birthday in 2019 is a Tuesday. Before September 2020 comes 29th February 2020, so her 6th birthday is 2 days on, a Thursday. Her 7th birthday in 2021 is a Friday.

stepByStep.text: The 6th birthday is on 3rd August 2015. No leap day comes in between, so it is 1 day on: a Monday.
The 7th birthday is on 3rd August 2016. We pass 29th February 2016, so it is 2 days on: a Wednesday.
The 8th birthday is on 3rd August 2017. It is 1 day on: a Thursday.
So the 8th birthday falls on a Thursday.

misconceptions.A: The 9th birthday, in 2018, is a Friday. Thursday comes one year earlier.
misconceptions.B: The 10th birthday, in 2019, is a Saturday. Count on year by year from 2014.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The birthdays fall on Monday, Wednesday and then Thursday, which is the 8th birthday.
misconceptions.D: The 7th birthday, in 2016, is a Wednesday. One more year reaches Thursday.

questionText: How many seconds are there in 2 hours?
hints: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 1 minute = 60 seconds.
1 hour = 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds.
2 hours = 2 × 3600 = 7200 seconds.

stepByStep.text: 1 hour = 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds
2 hours = 2 × 3600 = 7200 seconds

misconceptions.B: Multiplied 2 × 60 × 10 instead of 2 × 60 × 60
misconceptions.C: This is 1 hour in seconds, not 2

questionText: A normal year has how many odd days?
hints: A normal year has 365 days. Divide by 7 to find complete weeks and extra days.
365 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 1 day.
That 1 extra day is called 1 'odd day.' It's why the same date shifts by 1 day each normal year.

stepByStep.text: 365 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 1 day
Odd days = 1

misconceptions.B: 2 odd days is for a leap year (366 days)
misconceptions.C: 0 odd days means the day wouldn't change year to year (only true for 400-year cycles)
misconceptions.D: 7 would mean 0 odd days (7 is a full week)

questionText: In the year 2000, Gandhi Jayanti (2nd October) fell on Monday. In which year was it first celebrated on Sunday after 2000?
hints: We need to go backwards 1 day from Monday = Sunday, which means we need total odd days = 6 (or 7−1).

Odd days: 2000(2, leap), 2001(1), 2002(1), 2003(1), 2004(2, leap). After 2000: 2 odd days → Wed. After 2001: +1=3 → Thu. After 2002: +1=4 → Fri. After 2003: +1=5 → Sat. After 2004: +2=7=0 → Mon again. Hmm.

Wait: 2000→2001: 2 Oct falls after Feb, so the leap year effect depends on position. 2000: advance 1 (Oct is after Feb, only 1 odd day from Oct to Oct in a year where the leap day is BEFORE). Mon+1=Tue(2001). +1=Wed(2002). +1=Thu(2003). +2=Sat(2004, leap year crossed). +1=Sun(2005). ✓

stepByStep.text: 2 Oct 2000 = Monday
Year by year: 2001=Tue, 2002=Wed, 2003=Thu, 2004=Sat (leap year adds 2), 2005=Sun
First Sunday = 2005

misconceptions.A: 2004 = Saturday (close but not Sunday!)
misconceptions.B: 2003 = Thursday, not Sunday
misconceptions.D: 2006 = Monday (cycle restarts)
